we have found that the NPI cell monlayers, which were shortly exposed to microencapulated monolayer of ESCs in vitro, were accelerated in their maturation and differentiation to insulin producing β-cells, and that these β-cells expressed c-kit, a marker that is known to be involved in growth and differentiation of hematopoietic and other cell types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ESC/NPIs coculture system is a promising model for studying β-cell development and differentiation.
the coculturing of ESC with NPIs may provide a new approach for the production of insulin-producing cells from porcine islets.

the microencapsulated ESC coculture system may be used to accelerate maturation and/or differentiation of the NPEs cell monolayers and to identify an insulin-producing cell subpopulation that might be involved in the development of the β-cell phenotype.
